newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RTRS-Rugby union-All Blacks eye listing on NZ stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rugby union-All Blacks eye listing on NZ stock exchange.

text.p: The New Zealand Rugby Football Union's (NZRFU) board has spoken informally about listing the national side, the All Blacks, on the Stock Exchange, union chief executive David Moffett said on Tuesday.
The New Zealand Press Association reported that Moffett said rugby was "generally under-capitalised".
"It has been for some years and is even more so now that we have a professional rugby arm. It has been informally discussed by the board during our strategic review, but nothing more than that.
The matter is not on the agenda for Wednesday's NZRFU board meeting in Wellington.
The meeting will discuss the union's recommendation for the four to six players to be named as its "stars" for the transfer market.
"The players have been recommended by union staff and the criteria will be released tomorrow with the names," Moffett said.
The major task for the meeting is to consider the budget for 1997, which, according to Moffett, is looking vastly better than the estimated NZ$6 million loss recorded in the past year.
The board will also receive a briefing from International Rugby Board (IRB) members Rob Fisher and Tim Gresson.
